root_motivation: Joe's mcphost gate takes 21–42 minutes for a 413 s cold compile. The repo's `tests/` directory holds 289 top-level `.rs` files (2026-09-12 count) and cargo's default `autotests` makes each one a separate test binary; each links the whole 52K-LoC crate and its 41 dependencies, and measured binaries are 274–291 MB (`attrib_ac1_loopback_signup_unstamped`, `infer_ac08_ac09_python_requirements`). `target/debug/deps` holds 1,391 such binaries. 269 of the files declare `mod common;`, so the shared helper is compiled 269 times. RedBaron's root disk reached 81–86 % on 09-08, with `target/` dirs the known bulk. Every gate pays the link cost 289 times for one crate; every new AC PRD adds another binary. PRD-build-gate-phase-timing measures the `gate` phase this PRD moves; until it ships, the expected saving is inferred from binary count and size, not measured.
user_persona: The /build loop's own gate, which pays the cargo link cost for 289 near-identical test binaries every mcphost gate (21-42 min wall); secondarily the operator watching RedBaron's disk (81-86% on 09-08), the AC-pairing classifier needing unchanged test file paths, and a builder adding tests/<name>.rs who must be told if it never gets linked into a suite.

Given a new file `tests/zzz_ac1_probe.rs` that is not in any suite, When `gen-test-suites.sh --check` runs, Then it exits non-zero naming `tests/zzz_ac1_probe.rs`; after regenerating, it exits 0 and the test is listed.
Given the consolidated layout, When `grep -c 'mod common' tests/*.rs` runs over the included files, Then the count is 0 and each suite file declares `mod common;` once.

Given the archived mcphost PRDs' test pointers (for example `tests/hooks_ac1_*.rs`), When the verified-completed pairing classifier runs against them, Then every pairing that resolved before resolves now.
Given a clean `target/`, When `cargo nextest run` completes, Then `du -s target/debug/deps` is under 5 GB and the receipt records the size.

Given two timed full nextest runs at the same commit, one before and one after the change (or the `gate:` phase from PRD-build-gate-phase-timing when present), When compared in the receipt, Then the after time is ≤50 % of before.
Given `.config/nextest.toml` with JUnit enabled, When the suite runs, Then a JUnit file exists with a duration per test.
Given the parity script from mcphost-tests-host-independence, When run against the new layout on one host, Then it matches by test name and reports the same test count as before.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the `suite` selftest cases, When the repo's test selftest runs, Then they are named and green.

scope: Cargo.toml: `autotests = false`; one `[[test]]` per area with `path = "tests/suite_<area>_NN.rs"`; areas chosen by filename prefix so no suite exceeds roughly 60-80 files and the grand total (both sandbox/core partitions plus the exclusive-global singleton buckets) is <=10 (P0).

scripts/gen-test-suites.sh: scans top-level tests/*.rs, assigns each to an area by prefix table, writes tests/suite_<area>_NN.rs with `#[path = "<file>.rs"] mod <ident>;` lines plus one `mod common;` (and `support`/`ci_sandbox_support` where used); output is deterministic and sorted; `--check` exits non-zero naming any top-level tests/*.rs not included in a suite or any suite file that drifted from the generator's own output, wired into ci-test-partition.sh check / CI (P0).

Per-file `mod common;` (and the two other helper declarations) removed from included files and replaced by `use crate::common;` (or equivalent) so the helper compiles once per suite, not once per file; a test that names `common::` items unchanged still compiles (P0).

Every test that ran before runs after: nextest's test list, suite prefix stripped, equals the pre-change list; the verified-completed pairing classifier and intent-card test pointers resolve exactly as before since files stay where they are (P0).

Exclusive-global-subscriber isolation (2026-09-12 follow-up, CI red on plain `cargo test`): a handful of files that install a process-global tracing subscriber each get their own singleton `[[test]]` binary (distribute_exclusive in gen-test-suites.sh) rather than sharing a ~60-80-file bucket with unrelated tests, since cargo test's thread-per-test concurrency (unlike nextest's per-test process isolation) lets a concurrently-running unrelated test's log line pollute the exclusive test's captured-log buffer.
.config/nextest.toml emits JUnit with per-test timing so a later gate-phase-timing PRD can split the `gate` phase into per-test time (P1).
README section documenting how to add a test: drop the file, run the generator, or let CI tell you (P1).
non_goals: Changing any test's body or assertion, or any src/ file -- this PRD's whole diff is Cargo.toml, tests/suite_*.rs, the per-file mod-common/mod-ci_sandbox_support rewrite, and scripts/; verified every commit via `git diff --stat` showing zero src/ paths.

Changing the runner: nextest stays the test executor, and its per-test process isolation is exactly what keeps the mcphost-tests-host-independence fixes valid; only the test *binary* boundary moves, not the runner.
Reducing the number of test files -- consolidation is at the binary-link level only; every tests/<name>.rs file keeps its name, its path, and its own test functions.
Sharding suites across machines -- SANDBOX_SHARDS' existing 2-way CI matrix split is preserved unchanged, not extended or replaced.

additional.no_src_change: Engineering target explicitly scopes this PRD to Cargo.toml, tests/, and scripts/ only; every commit this PRD landed (07db1f4, d40b1a3, and the earlier extend-scaffold/bump/changelog/intent-card-refresh commits) shows zero files under src/ in `git diff --stat`.
additional.test_identity_preserved: gen-test-suites.sh's `#[path]`-inclusion keeps every test's file and name identical (module identifiers derive from the unchanged file stem); `cargo nextest list`'s test-name set, suite prefix stripped, must equal the pre-consolidation set (AC1's guardrail) -- verified via a clean `cargo test --tests`/`cargo nextest run` both green at 602/602 with 0 failures post-change.
additional.max_ten_binaries: The generator's per-partition MAX_PER_SUITE (core=80, sandbox=60, split 2026-09-12 to absorb the exclusive-global singleton-bucket overhead without touching sandbox's CI-load-bearing 2-shard split) plus the 5 exclusive-global singleton buckets must not exceed 10 total [[test]] binaries end to end (AC1); currently exactly 10 (3 core normal + 5 core singleton + 2 sandbox).
additional.run_metrics_ac_counter_stays_accurate: scripts/run-metrics.sh's project-local AC-counting fallback (owner-map.json explicitly permits project-local fixes to this fallback, folded back via postmortem) must correctly count tests/ac<NN>_*.rs pass/fail under the new module-qualified `test <stem>::<fn> ... ok` output shape introduced by consolidation, not just the old per-binary `Running tests/<stem>.rs` / `test result: ok.` shape it originally shipped with -- fixed in this PRD's own diff (both matchers now coexist) after reviewer-agent caught the fallback silently pinned at 0/19 across four consecutive commits.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does mcphost's gate take 21-42 minutes for a 413s cold compile?
five_whys_trace.a: The repo's tests/ directory holds 289 top-level .rs files and cargo's default `autotests` makes each one its own integration-test binary; each links the whole 52K-LoC crate and its 41 dependencies (measured binaries 274-291 MB), so the gate pays the link cost 289 times for one crate.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the crate get relinked 289 times instead of a handful?
five_whys_trace.a: Nothing in Cargo.toml overrides cargo's own one-binary-per-top-level-test-file convention (`autotests` defaults on with no `[[test]]` entries grouping files), and 269 of the 289 files separately declare `mod common;`, so the shared test helper is also compiled 269 times.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does this matter enough to fix now rather than let it keep growing?
five_whys_trace.a: RedBaron's root disk reached 81-86% on 2026-09-08 with target/ dirs the known bulk (target/debug/deps holding 1,391 such binaries across projects), and every new AC PRD on this repo adds one more 280MB binary to that pile plus another 289th of link time to every future gate.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is this framed as a proactive fix rather than a failure investigation?
five_whys_trace.a: Per the PRD's own why-chain note, this is not a response to a specific failure -- it acts on leaf 1 of the vision doc's 2026-09-12 gate-cost section (the assumption that binary count/size drives gate wall time), which PRD-build-gate-phase-timing will independently verify once its own `gate:` phase-seconds field ships; until then the expected saving is measured directly in this PRD's own before/after receipt (docs/benchmarks/suite-consolidation-wall-time.txt: 1405s -> 139s, 9.9% of before).

ambiguities_resolved.question: The findings file records the reference Python client seeing well-formed ttlMs/cacheScope on an unauthenticated tools/list, which the code says is impossible. Which is right?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Almost certainly a client-side deserialization default printed where the wire had nothing (rmcp's own mirror of that shape defaults to ttl_ms 0 / cache_scope Private). Settled by a test rather than an argument: AC2 asserts on the serialized wire JSON, not a deserialized model.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Requirement 9 offers two ways to fix the middleware doc/scope mismatch: re-scope the layer to /mcp, or correct the comment to say it is router-wide. Which?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Correct the comment. It is the smaller behavioural change, and an unauthenticated health endpoint carrying an accurate protocol-version header is harmless.
